Subject: Operator eviction requirement and zeroize expectations for BYOK HSM

Hi Monica,

Thanks again for the demo last week. A quick follow-up from our security team: for our private deployment (VPC/on-prem) we need a clear operator-eviction and zeroize protocol for BYOK workflows. The asks are fairly tight:

- Immediate key zeroize on operator removal (within 5 minutes SLA)
- Proof-of-wipe artifacts (audit log & signed statement)
- No plaintext key material persisted on the host after eviction
- A test window we can observe and sign off on

Can Redwood provide an architecture diagram plus a runbook we can validate in our staging environment? If you can include a short script to simulate operator eviction that would speed our review.

Appreciate it — target for our compliance board is 2027-05-27.

Thanks,
Lilly Park
Sr. Security Engineer, Acme Corp

Attachments: acme-signed-requirements-20270514.pdf (pdf, 280KB)

From: monica_patel@redwood.ai

Date: Mon, 17 May 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Operator eviction requirement and zeroize expectations for BYOK HSM

Lilly — thanks for the clear requirements. Attaching a first-draft runbook and a PoC eviction script. High-level summary below and then the runbook has step-by-step checks.

Summary (high-level):
- Ephemeral wrapping keys: we recommend wrapping customer BYOK in an ephemeral wrapping key managed by an HSM module; the wrapping key has a short TTL and is bound to the operator pod identity.
- Eviction flow: operator removal triggers (1) orchestration action to revoke operator identity, (2) HSM policy to zeroize ephemeral wrapping key, (3) agent process scrub of any in-memory caches and ephemeral files, (4) audit record creation and signed attestation from HSM.
- Evidence: signed HSM attestation + orchestration event id + host syscall logs (safeguarded via host-local secure logging agent).
- SLA: target zeroize completion within 5 minutes; proof artifact available within 10 minutes.

See attached: redwood_draft_zeroize_runbook_v1.pdf and eviction-proof-of-concept.sh.

Proposed next steps:
1) Quick sync (30m) this week to walk the runbook — Wed or Thu?
2) Schedule a staged eviction test in your staging VPC; we can provide a remote observer role.
3) Collect feedback and produce a compliance package for your board.

If that sounds good I'll loop in infra to confirm the test window.

—Monica
Monica Patel
Senior Product Manager, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_draft_zeroize_runbook_v1.pdf (pdf), eviction-proof-of-concept.sh (shell script)

Monica — quick architecture note from infra/runtime: we need to call out network topology constraints for the attestation and audit upload. A few concerns: 

- If the HSM is on-prem with air-gapped egress restrictions, the signed attestation must be retrievable over an internal secure channel; our design uses a host-side log forwarder that writes to a customer-controlled S3/MinIO endpoint. We need a fallback when outbound is restricted.
- The zeroize command path should be executed inside the HSM enclave if possible; otherwise the HSM must provide a signed audit that can be validated without contacting Redwood cloud.
- We should add a step to scrub any swap/file-system swap traces and to forcibly unmap memory pages in the operator process. There are slight differences between Linux kernel versions — attach a kernel compatibility checklist.

I'll mark these on the runbook draft and add a small test harness to the PoC script that demonstrates both egress and local-archive modes.

—Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
Principal Infrastructure Engineer
Redwood Inference

Thanks all — I pushed an update to the runbook (section 4.2) to include ephemeral key-wrapping TTLs and an optional hardware-backed monotonic counter in the HSM for replay protection. A few practical notes for the staging test:

- We'll run two scenarios: (A) eviction with normal egress (upload attestation to customer staging bucket) and (B) eviction in egress-restricted mode (persist signed artifact locally and ship via out-of-band transfer you control).
- During the test, the operator VM will be forcibly terminated to validate that the zeroize still runs (we rely on HSM-side policy enforcement for the final destroy).
- I added a checklist item to verify that no VM snapshots exist post-eviction (customer ops must confirm snapshot policy is disabled for test VMs).

Proposed test windows: Thu 20 May 14:00-17:00 PST or Fri 21 May 09:00-12:00 PST. Which works for you?

Tessa Morgan
